t: This is the area of Mount Pleasant in Clerkenwell where Coldbath Fields Prison once stood. It was founded in the reign of James I, completely rebuilt in 1794, extended in 1850, and closed in 1885. It held prisoners on short sentences of up to two years, and people called it the Steel. Two men are recorded as dying here. Edward Dando was a thief, famous for eating his fill at food stalls and inns and then admitting he couldn't pay. William Dugdale was a publisher and bookseller of subversive and pornographic works, who spent many years in prison.
